desc:
PrestaShop integrations for shipping and accounting connect your shop to the tools that run your orders. Ecom Swift LLC installs or builds the connection, maps the data and tests it with sample orders, so you stop retyping.

## What are PrestaShop integrations?

A PrestaShop integration is a connection that moves data between your shop and another system without anyone copying it by hand. Common examples are a shipping carrier that receives orders and returns tracking numbers, accounting software that receives invoices, a marketplace such as Amazon or eBay that shares stock and orders, and a payment provider that reports payment status.

Some integrations use a module from the PrestaShop add-on ecosystem. Others use an API and a small custom link when no module fits.

## Why manual order handling gets expensive

When tools do not talk to each other, a person fills the gap. Someone retypes an order into a shipping portal, copies an invoice into the ledger, or updates stock on a marketplace after every sale. This is slow and quiet work, and it fails in a predictable way: a typo on an address, an order forgotten over a weekend, a product that sells on two channels when only one unit is left.

Each mistake costs time to correct and sometimes costs a customer. Connecting the systems removes the repeated step, so staff time goes to work that needs judgment.

## How integrations affect your results

Good integrations save time, reduce errors and make stock numbers trustworthy. When an order reaches the carrier automatically, labels print faster and tracking reaches the customer sooner. When stock updates flow between PrestaShop and a marketplace, you are less likely to oversell. When invoices reach accounting without retyping, the books are easier to close.

The effect depends on volume. A shop with a few orders a week gains a little time. A shop with daily orders across several channels gains much more. We describe the benefit as saved effort and fewer mistakes, not as extra sales.

## What a well-built integration includes

- A maintained module where one exists, so updates and support come from its author.
- A custom connection only where no suitable module is available.
- Field mapping agreed with you, covering products, customers, addresses and taxes.
- Clear rules for which system holds the master copy of stock and prices.
- Order status updates sent in both directions where the tool supports it.
- Error alerts by email, so a failed sync does not go unseen.
- A retry setup for syncs that fail on a temporary fault.
- Testing with sample orders, including awkward cases such as partial shipments.
- A written note describing what moves, when, and where to look if it stops.

## How we work

First we agree on the tools to connect and what should move between them. We check whether a maintained PrestaShop module covers the need. If it does, we install and configure it. If not, we write a small custom link using PrestaShop hooks and the other tool's API.

We map fields with you, then test with sample orders in a safe setting before connecting live data. The Basic package connects one tool. Standard connects two, with stock rules, two-way order status and an error alert. Premium connects up to three tools, includes a custom link if needed, sets up retries for failed syncs and ends with a handover call.

You pay the other tools directly. Our price covers the connection work only.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which system is the source of truth for stock before connecting anything.
- Keep a list of every carrier, marketplace and accounting tool you use.
- Test with a low-value order before processing real shipments.
- Keep product codes and tax settings consistent across systems.
- Read the setup note so you know where to check when a sync fails.

**Avoid:**
- Connecting two tools that both try to edit the same stock number.
- Installing several modules that do the same job.
- Syncing every product field when only a few are needed.
- Ignoring error emails because the shop still seems to work.
- Changing tax or carrier settings without checking the connected tools.

## Who this is for

This service suits shops that ship daily and want labels and tracking without retyping. It suits sellers that list on a marketplace and need stock to stay in step. It also suits owners whose bookkeeper asks for invoices in a certain format every month.

## How to get started

Send us the names of the tools you want connected and a description of what should move between them. Give us staff or developer access to PrestaShop, and ask the other tool to add us as a team user where it allows it. We never need your passwords. We reply with a short checklist, then build, test and hand over with notes.
